name: IM-1 Odysseus
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Local sunset at the south-polar site; lander tipped on a 12-degree slope, one solar panel lit; not designed to survive lunar night
reported_note: Intuitive Machines sent lunar-night configuration commands at about noon US Eastern on 2024-02-29 (~17:00 UTC; approximate) as the Sun fell out of view of the one illuminated solar panel; power depleted shortly after. Lander was in final hours on 02-28. The Sun set about a week after landing (7 days). Wake attempts from 2024-03-20 failed; declared over 2024-03-23.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram / Pragyan)
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Lander put into sleep mode around 08:00 IST on 2023-09-04 as local sunset approached (electronics not rated for -120 C night); rover parked 2023-09-02
reported_note: Landing 18:03-18:04 IST (12:33-12:34 UTC; sources differ by a minute). Pragyan rover set to sleep 2023-09-02; Vikram lander ~08:00 IST (02:30 UTC) 2023-09-04, about 12 days after landing, 'when darkness fell'. ISRO hoped to wake them 2023-09-22 at next sunrise; no response by 2023-09-28. Exact local sunset time not published; end_utc is the sleep command time.

name: SLIM
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Landed in an attitude where solar cells faced west and generated no power; battery shut down by ground command ~2.6 h after landing to avoid over-discharge
reported_note: First end of operations (JAXA: shutdown 02:57 JST 2024-01-20 = 17:57 UTC 01-19). Contact regained ~2024-01-28 (JST) when sunlight reached the west-facing cells; SLIM then survived three lunar nights (woke 2024-02-25, 2024-03-27, 2024-04-23), last contact 2024-04-28/29, attempts ended 2024-08-26 as the Sun set at the site. Designed for one lunar day only. Replay should use the initial anomaly or the late-April final sunset (last_contact_utc).

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Lunar sunset on 2025-03-16; solar-powered lander operated about 5 hours into the lunar night until batteries depleted
reported_note: Firefly: just over 5 h of operation after lunar sunset; final data received ~6:15 pm CDT 2025-03-16 (= 23:15 UTC; Wikipedia states 23:25 UTC). Sunset therefore ~18:15 UTC (derived, not stated by Firefly; NASA only says March 16). 346 h of daylight, >14 days on surface. Landing time 08:34 UTC per Wikipedia (3:34 am CST).

name: IM-2 Athena
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Lander came to rest on its side in a shadowed crater; solar arrays could not generate enough power and batteries were depleted <13 h after landing
reported_note: Not a sunset end: Athena tipped over, ~250 m from the target, in a shadowed crater (about -173 C); power 'fully depleted', last contact 06:15 UTC 2025-03-07 (1:15 am EST per NASA). Landing time 17:28:50 UTC per Wikipedia infobox (collectSPACE: ~12:30 pm EST); sources differ by about a minute. Sunset time not stated.

name: HAKUTO-R Mission 2 (Resilience)
coord_source: LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile) https://data.lroc.im-ldi.com/lroc/view_rdr/SHAPEFILE_ANTHROPOGENIC_OBJECTS
end_reason: Crashed (hard landing) during landing attempt; no surface operations
reported_note: Landing attempt 2025-06-05 19:17 UTC; telemetry showed fast descent and contact was lost shortly before touchdown. Coordinates are the LROC-identified impact crater. Not usable for sunset validation; listed for completeness.
